prompt: A two-column proof begins with the given equation $3x - 7 = 20$. Step 2 adds $7$ to both sides (Addition Property of Equality). Step 3 divides both sides by $3$ (Division Property of Equality). What value of $x$ does the proof reach?
hint: The proof names two operations in order. Carry out each one on both sides of the equation.

hints.text: The proof names two operations in order. Carry out each one on both sides of the equation.
Adding $7$ to both sides of $3x - 7 = 20$ gives $3x = 27$. Now do the division that step 3 describes.
$27 \div 3 = 9$, so the proof reaches the value $x = 9$.

explanation: Step 2 uses the Addition Property of Equality: adding $7$ to both sides gives $3x - 7 + 7 = 20 + 7$, so $3x = 27$.
Step 3 uses the Division Property of Equality: dividing both sides by $3$ gives $x = 9$.
Substituting back gives $3(9) - 7 = 27 - 7 = 20$, so the proof correctly reaches $x = 9$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why proofs name the properties
steps: Solving an equation IS a proof — each move is legal because a property of equality says so.
Adding 7 to both sides is the Addition Property; dividing both sides by 3 is the Division Property. Naming them is what turns arithmetic into an argument.
